summary: Smoke verification after backend supervisor restart. No 502 errors from external URL. Backend auth (request-code + verify with test@copythat.app / 246810), /api/settings, /api/courses, /api/scanner all return 200 with bearer token (401 without, as expected). Web app loads, email/code login works, archive lists 5 courses (7 course-testID elements), course detail page opens, and Settings page renders with scanner-card visible. 502 issue is resolved.
critical_code_review_comments: supervisor backend program has autostart=false (per handoff note); any future pod restart will again leave backend STOPPED and reproduce the 502. Consider flipping autostart=true in supervisor config so backend recovers automatically on pod restart.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login via POST /api/auth/verify returns the JWT in the field named 'token' (not 'access_token'). Use Bearer <token> header. Test account test@copythat.app with static code 246810 works end-to-end. Backend supervisor program is autostart=false — if 502 reappears after a pod restart, run `sudo supervisorctl start backend` before debugging.
rca_of_issue: RCA (from handoff, confirmed by observation): backend supervisor program has autostart=false and config is read-only; after a pod restart it stayed STOPPED, so Kubernetes ingress 502'd every /api request. Mitigation: `sudo supervisorctl start backend` (already done; `supervisorctl status` now shows backend RUNNING). All 4 target endpoints verified returning 200 via EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.
